title: Auto Runtime configuration file
description: The settings of Auto Runtime that are lists or maps, where Studio comes from, a declared local mode, the usage ping, payload offloading and the license, read from the file that CONFIG_FILE names. Each key stands for the environment variable of the same name in upper case, which wins over it, and license for AUTO_RUNTIME_LICENSE, whose key and allocation AUTO_RUNTIME_LICENSE_KEY and AUTO_RUNTIME_ALLOCATION win over. Secrets are written as references such as ${GATEWAY_API_KEY}.

allowed_origins.description: The origins a page in a browser may call the API from, such as https://app.example.com. ALLOWED_ORIGINS wins over it

studio_origin.description: The origin Studio is served from, an https URL, or an http URL on localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], with no path; a page there may call the API, and the runtime fetches Studio from it when it serves Studio. https://studio.on.auto when left out. STUDIO_ORIGIN wins over it

serve_studio.description: Whether the runtime serves Studio itself at /studio/ on its own address, fetched from the Studio host and kept, since a page on a public address may not reach an address on the machine. On in local mode and off otherwise when left out. SERVE_STUDIO wins over it

webhook_url.description: The public https URL of this runtime, as services outside your network reach it, with no path, such as https://runtime.example.com. Auto gives a connection's service an address under it when it asks the service to send a webhook as soon as something happens there. Leave it unset if nothing outside can reach the runtime: Auto then checks the service on a timer. WEBHOOK_URL wins over it

access_mode.description: local declares local mode, where every request acts as the local developer with no credential, for a runtime whose port only this computer reaches, such as a container whose port is published on 127.0.0.1 alone. It takes no API_KEYS, and a PUBLIC_URL only on localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], which names the address of the runtime and signs no one in; a runtime that listens beyond the loopback needs that PUBLIC_URL. ACCESS_MODE wins over it

name.description: The provider prefix, such as gateway in gateway/llama-3.3-70b: 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter, unique, and not a built-in prefix

base_url.description: The http or https URL that /chat/completions is appended to, such as https://gateway.example.com/v1

api_key.description: The key, sent as Authorization: Bearer <key>; in the configuration file a reference such as ${GATEWAY_API_KEY}

headers.description: Headers sent with every request, their values treated as secrets; in the configuration file a credential is a reference

query_params.description: Query parameters added to every request, their values treated as secrets

structured_outputs.description: true when the endpoint accepts response_format json_schema; otherwise no response_format is sent, the schema of a JSON answer is written into the instructions, and the answer is checked here. Default false

include_usage.description: Asks for usage in streamed responses. Default false

expose_provider_messages.description: true when the gateway's error messages are safe to show to callers of a reasoning function. Default false

allowed_provider_options.description: The top-level request body fields a reasoning function may set for this gateway through provider_options, such as user and metadata. Default none

cost_header.description: A gateway entry names the header its gateway answers the call's cost in, in US dollars, or names none and no cost is kept. A run keeps the cost as cost_usd

model_gateways.description: OpenAI-compatible gateways, each a provider prefix of its own. MODEL_GATEWAYS wins over it

model_aliases.description: Model references a reasoning function may give, each sent on as another reference; a trailing * on both sides covers every model of a provider. MODEL_ALIASES wins over it

items.description: A model id as the provider receives it, such as eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0

declared_models.description: The models list_models shows for bedrock, bedrock-anthropic, azure, vertex and vertex-anthropic, which do not list their own, and for a gateway whose list cannot be read, keyed by the provider prefix. DECLARED_MODELS wins over it

items.description: A model reference a reasoning function may give, written provider/model, or provider/* for every model of a provider

allowed_models.description: The only model references a reasoning function may give, by name or through an alias, and list_models shows, each provider/model or provider/* for every model of a provider; every model when left out. ALLOWED_MODELS wins over it

voice_model.description: The model that writes out what a person says, which Studio offers beside each comment field, as provider/model, its provider openai or the name of an entry of model_gateways, such as openai/whisper-1; none when left out. VOICE_MODEL wins over it

type.description: mcp for a remote MCP server, given url; stdio for an MCP server this server starts as a process, given command; openapi for an HTTP API, given document. Taken from url, command or document when left out

url.description: The http or https URL of a remote MCP server, spoken to over Streamable HTTP

headers.description: Headers sent to a remote MCP server, or to an HTTP API outside its document's security schemes, with every request; the value of a reference such as ${GRAPH_API_KEY} is a secret, scrubbed from everything a call records, and a value written out is not

issuer.description: The issuer of the authorization server the credential was registered with, pinned: it is sent to no other. An https URL, or an http URL on a loopback address

client_id.description: The client id registered with that authorization server

client_secret.description: The client secret, as a reference such as ${GRAPH_CLIENT_SECRET}

private_key.description: A private key in PEM that signs the client assertion, as a reference such as ${GRAPH_PRIVATE_KEY}

algorithm.description: The signing algorithm of private_key, such as RS256 or ES256

scope.description: The scopes to ask for, separated by spaces

discovery.description: How an mcp server's authorization server is found: protected_resource, the default, from the server's protected-resource metadata, which must name the issuer first; issuer, from the issuer itself, for a server whose metadata names another authorization server first, such as a gateway that signs people in itself. With issuer the server is not asked to name the issuer, so check that url is the server these credentials are for

audience.description: For an authorization server that names the API a token is for by an audience: the identifier the API is registered under there. Auto then asks for a token for that audience, not for this server's address. The token is sent to this server, so name the API it serves

grant.description: How Auto asks for a token. client_credentials, the default, asks for a token for the client itself. jwt_bearer asks with a JWT that private_key signs, as RFC 7523 sets out, for the account subject names, as a service account does. It takes private_key with its algorithm and subject, and no client_secret

subject.description: With grant jwt_bearer, the account the token is asked for, such as the mailbox a service account works in

auth.description: OAuth client credentials, for a server whose authorization server issues tokens to clients: client_secret, or private_key with its algorithm. An mcp server's authorization server is found from the server's own metadata, or from the issuer's where discovery is issuer; an openapi server's from the issuer's. With grant jwt_bearer, Auto asks for a token for the account subject names

command.description: The command of a stdio server: an installed, pinned program, never a package downloaded at start such as npx -y

args.description: The arguments of the command of a stdio server

env.description: The whole environment of the process of a stdio server, which inherits nothing else; the value of a reference such as ${GRAPH_API_KEY} is a secret, scrubbed from everything a call records, and a value written out is not

document.description: The OpenAPI document of an HTTP API, version 3.0, 3.1 or 3.2, read once at start: an https URL, an http URL on a loopback address, or a path relative to the directory of the configuration file

base_url.description: The URL the calls of an HTTP API go to, in place of the first server its document names; required when it names none. An https URL, or an http URL on a loopback address

query_params.description: Query parameters sent to an HTTP API with every call, outside its document's security schemes, such as a tenant; the value of a reference such as ${GRAPH_API_KEY} is a secret, scrubbed from everything a call records, and a value written out is not

security.description: The credential of each security scheme of an HTTP API's document the entry gives, by the scheme's name, placed as the scheme says: an apiKey in its header or query parameter, a bearer as Authorization: Bearer, a basic as user:password; an oauth2 or openIdConnect scheme takes the auth block instead; each value is a reference such as ${BILLING_API_KEY} or ada:${BILLING_PASSWORD}, a secret, and one written out is refused

succeeded.description: A JSON pointer to the boolean of a JSON answer that says whether the call succeeded, false for a failure, such as /ok

code.description: A JSON pointer to the string of a failed answer that names its failure, such as /error

key_refused.description: The codes that say the API refused the credential, as a 401 says elsewhere

scope_lacking.description: The codes that say the credential lacks a scope the call needs

rate_limited.description: The codes that say the API limits the rate of its calls, as a 429 says elsewhere

failure_codes.description: For an HTTP API that answers a failure in a JSON answer of a successful status: where the answer says whether the call succeeded and the code that names its failure, and the codes that mean a refused credential, a lacking scope or a limited rate; any other failed answer is an error result carrying the answer

org.description: The org this server serves, a list of orgs, or * for every org of this server, required; one entry serves each org it names under one name, with one credential and one connection

playbooks.description: The playbooks this server serves within each org it names, by id; every playbook of each org when left out, and refused beside * for every org

allowed.description: The tools of this server a function may name, each named as the server lists it; every tool of the server when left out

reads.description: The tools that only read, each named as the server lists it

acts.description: The tools that may change something, each named as the server lists it

marks.description: The mark of each tool named, which wins over the one the server's hints or the HTTP method of an operation give: reads for a tool that only reads, acts for one that may change something; a tool named in neither keeps the mark it is listed with, and one nothing marks is unmarked, which counts as one that may change something. A name the server does not list is ignored

record_content.description: Whether the arguments and the answers of this server's calls are kept whole, scrubbed of secrets, in the playbook's ledger, where anyone who may read the playbook reads them; false keeps their sizes alone. Default true

handles_money.description: Whether the tools of this server pay, refund, transfer or pay out money; the directory listing does not offer such a server. Default false

request_id.description: The response header, or for an MCP server the key of the metadata of a result, in which the server carries its own id of a request, recorded with each call

provider.description: A provider the runtime knows, by its name, which gives the server and where its credential goes: the entry then gives placeholders, credential, org, playbooks, allowed and record_content, and no field of the server

placeholders.description: With provider, the value of each of the provider's placeholders, by name, never a reference

anyOf.description: For a secret, a reference such as ${TRACKER_TOKEN}

kind.description: The way of the provider the credential takes, when not its first

value.description: For a secret, a reference such as ${TRACKER_TOKEN}

client_id.description: For client credentials, the client id, written out

client_secret.description: For client credentials, a reference such as ${LEDGERS_CLIENT_SECRET}

private_key.description: For client credentials, a private key in PEM as a reference such as ${LEDGERS_PRIVATE_KEY}

algorithm.description: The signing algorithm of private_key, such as RS256 or ES256

credential.description: With provider, the credential of the way kind names, or else of its first way but authorization, a consent a person gives on Studio's page alone: a secret as a reference such as ${TRACKER_TOKEN}, or client credentials as the client id written out with client_secret, or with private_key and its algorithm, each key a reference; nothing for a way that takes none

tool_servers.description: The tool servers whose tools a function may name, each bound to an org and optionally its playbooks: url for a remote MCP server, command for an MCP server run as a process, document for an HTTP API described by an OpenAPI document. Secrets are references such as ${GRAPH_API_KEY}. TOOL_SERVERS wins over it

people_may_add.description: Whether people may add connections through their agents; true when left out

allowed_hosts.description: The hosts a connection may reach, each a host or *. and a host for every host under it; a loopback, private or link-local address is reached only where it is named here by itself, and a name that resolves to one never is; every host that is none of those addresses when left out

credential_kinds.description: The kinds of credential a connection may take, of none, reference, secret, client_credentials, authorization and jwt_bearer; every kind when left out

variables.description: The variables of the runtime a reference credential may name, never one the runtime reads for itself; none when left out, so no connection takes a reference

issuers.description: The issuers of the authorization servers the client is registered at, each an https URL, or an http URL on a loopback address; one written with a placeholder, such as https://login.example.com/{tenant}, is kept as it is written

client_id.description: The client id the authorization servers issued

client_secret.description: The client secret, as a reference such as ${EXAMPLE_CLIENT_SECRET}

private_key.description: A private key in PEM that signs the client assertion, as a reference such as ${EXAMPLE_PRIVATE_KEY}

algorithm.description: The signing algorithm of private_key, such as RS256 or ES256

token_endpoint_auth_method.description: How the client authenticates at the token endpoint where the metadata of the authorization server leaves the choice; chosen from the client and the metadata when left out

scopes.description: The scopes the client may ask at its issuers, each as a provider's way writes it: a consent takes the first client at its issuer that names every scope it asks, the scope of the way at a first consent, and with a group of the way's more the scopes the connection holds and the group's. Named for each client where several clients serve one issuer, and left out for a client that may ask any

registered_clients.description: The clients whoever runs the runtime registered at authorization servers, each with the issuers it is registered at, its client_id, and its client_secret, or its private_key with its algorithm, as a reference, or neither for a public client, and the scopes it may ask, which each client names where several serve one issuer

auto_clients.description: Whether a provider whose way takes a registered client takes Auto's client too, through Auto's consent service, where no client registered at its issuer covers the scope the way asks; true in local mode and false otherwise when left out. AUTO_CLIENTS wins over it

name.description: The name of the provider and of a connection to it by default: 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter

aliases.description: Other names the provider is found by, such as a name it had before: a connection added under one is read as made from this provider, and none is listed

title.description: What a person reads as its name

description.description: What a function may do through it, in one or two sentences of at most 300 characters

summary.description: What playbooks can do through it, in one sentence of at most 120 characters, which a person reads under its title where they connect it; description stays what an agent reads

website.description: The https page where a person reads about the server and makes a credential

type.description: mcp for an MCP server, given url; openapi for an HTTP API

url.description: For mcp, the https URL of the server, {name} standing for the placeholder name

document.description: For openapi, the https URL of its OpenAPI document, {name} standing for the placeholder name

base_url.description: For openapi, the https URL its calls go to where the document names no server, {name} standing for the placeholder name

headers.description: Headers sent with every request, never a credential; a reference such as ${ADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN} stands for a value of whoever runs the runtime

query_params.description: For openapi, query parameters sent with every call, never a credential; a reference such as ${ADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN} stands for a value of whoever runs the runtime

request_id.description: The response header, or for an MCP server the key of the metadata of a result, in which the server carries its own id of a request, recorded with each call

handles_money.description: true for a provider whose tools pay, refund, transfer or pay out money, which the directory listing does not offer

reads.description: The tools that only read, each named as the server lists it

acts.description: The tools that may change something, each named as the server lists it

marks.description: The mark of each tool named, for the tools the server marks wrongly or not at all: reads for a tool that only reads, acts for one that may change something, each named as the server lists it; for openapi, a tool of the document beside the entries

succeeded.description: A JSON pointer to the boolean of a JSON answer that says whether the call succeeded, false for a failure, such as /ok

code.description: A JSON pointer to the string of a failed answer that names its failure, such as /error

key_refused.description: The codes that say the API refused the credential, as a 401 says elsewhere

scope_lacking.description: The codes that say the credential lacks a scope the call needs

rate_limited.description: The codes that say the API limits the rate of its calls, as a 429 says elsewhere

failure_codes.description: For openapi, an API that answers a failure in a JSON answer of a successful status: the pointers to whether the call succeeded and to the code of its failure, and the codes that mean a refused credential, a lacking scope or a limited rate

tell.description: The provider's practice, and what a person is told through it by a function that writes no tell: all where one more message is expected, as in a chat, so a reply taken is marked and answered, a reply not taken is answered and a request that ends says so; refusals where each message costs, as in mail or a text message, so only a reply that could not be taken is answered

tool.description: The tool that posts a message in the conversation of a person's reply, named as the server lists it

with.description: Its arguments, written as the arguments of a function's deliver are, each a Liquid template over to, sent.conversation, sent.id, message, reply.id and reply.to: message is the line, and reply.to the message the person's reply answers

sent.description: A JSON Pointer into what the tool answered, to the id of the message it posted

reply.description: How a line is posted in reply to a person

tool.description: The tool that marks a person's message with a reaction, named as the server lists it

with.description: Its arguments, written as the arguments of a function's deliver are, each a Liquid template over to, sent.conversation, sent.id, message, reply.id and reply.to

react.description: How a person's message is marked

tool.description: The tool that shows that Auto is working, named as the server lists it

with.description: Its arguments, written as the arguments of a function's deliver are, each a Liquid template over to, sent.conversation, sent.id, message, reply.id and reply.to

refused.description: The codes the tool answers when the service does not show this sign for the account at all, such as for a scope the credential lacks or a feature that is turned off

typing.description: How the provider shows a person that Auto is working on their reply

quota.description: The most reads of a conversation the service takes in one window

window_seconds.description: The window, in seconds, from 1 to 86400

clients.description: The client sources whose connections the service limits so, where it limits some apps and not others; left out, every connection

read_limit.description: How often the service lets the replies of a conversation be read, as a rate limit's quota and window: at most quota reads in each window. The runtime reads a conversation no sooner than the window divided by the quota after its last read, on its timer and when the service tells it of a message alike

automatic.description: A JSON Pointer within a message the reading tool lists, to what it holds only when an app posted it or it was sent automatically; such a message is passed over, never taken, refused or answered

conversations.description: How the provider's conversations are replied to and marked, for a function that asks a person through it and reads their replies

tool.description: The tool that posts a message in the thread of a person's message, named as the server lists it

with.description: Its arguments, written as the arguments of a function's deliver are. Each one is a Liquid template that can read these of the person's message: id, conversation, sender, thread where the message is in a thread, and kind, which is mention, direct_message or ambient. It can also read message, the words Auto posts, and rendered, the same message laid out as the service takes it, where the message has more than words. An argument whose template renders omit, as {{ thread | default: omit }} does for a message in no thread, is left out of the call.

sent.description: A JSON Pointer into what the tool answered, to the id of the message it posted

tool.description: The tool that replaces the words of a message Auto posted, named as the server lists it

with.description: Its arguments, written as the arguments of a function's deliver are. Each one is a Liquid template that can read these of the person's message: id, conversation, sender, thread where the message is in a thread, and kind, which is mention, direct_message or ambient. It can also read message, the words Auto posts, and rendered, the same message laid out as the service takes it, where the message has more than words. An argument whose template renders omit, as {{ thread | default: omit }} does for a message in no thread, is left out of the call. Its arguments can also read sent.id, the message Auto posted.

replace.description: How Auto turns a message it posted, such as one that says it is working, into its answer

answer.description: How Auto posts its answer in the thread of a person's message

tool.description: The tool that posts a line only one person sees, named as the server lists it

with.description: Its arguments, written as the arguments of a function's deliver are. Each one is a Liquid template that can read these of the person's message: id, conversation, sender, thread where the message is in a thread, and kind, which is mention, direct_message or ambient. It can also read message, the words Auto posts, and rendered, the same message laid out as the service takes it, where the message has more than words. An argument whose template renders omit, as {{ thread | default: omit }} does for a message in no thread, is left out of the call.

ephemeral.description: How Auto posts a line that only the person who wrote the message sees, where the provider has such a message

tool.description: The tool that reads the messages of a thread, named as the server lists it

with.description: Its arguments, written as the arguments of a function's deliver are. Each one is a Liquid template that can read these of the person's message: id, conversation, sender, thread where the message is in a thread, and kind, which is mention, direct_message or ambient. It can also read message, the words Auto posts, and rendered, the same message laid out as the service takes it, where the message has more than words. An argument whose template renders omit, as {{ thread | default: omit }} does for a message in no thread, is left out of the call.

list.description: A JSON Pointer into what the tool answered, to the thread's messages

order.description: The order the tool lists them in

id.description: A JSON Pointer within each message to its identity

sender.description: A JSON Pointer within each message to who wrote it

text.description: A JSON Pointer within each message to its words

time.description: A JSON Pointer within each message to when it was written: RFC 3339 text, or seconds since the epoch

automatic.description: A JSON Pointer within each message to what it holds only when an app posted it

read.description: Where, in what the tool answered, the thread's messages are

thread.description: How Auto reads the messages of the thread a person wrote in

tool.description: The tool that reads a person at the service, named as the server lists it

with.description: Its arguments, written as the arguments of a function's deliver are. Each one is a Liquid template that can read these of the person's message: id, conversation, sender, thread where the message is in a thread, and kind, which is mention, direct_message or ambient. It can also read message, the words Auto posts, and rendered, the same message laid out as the service takes it, where the message has more than words. An argument whose template renders omit, as {{ thread | default: omit }} does for a message in no thread, is left out of the call.

email.description: A JSON Pointer into what the tool answered, to the person's email address

email_verified.description: A JSON Pointer to the boolean that is true where the service confirmed that the address is the person's. Where it is left out, Auto counts no address as confirmed, and asks each person to sign in instead.

account.description: A JSON Pointer to the id of the account the person belongs to, such as a workspace

name.description: A JSON Pointer into what the tool answered, to the person's name. Auto shows this name on the page where the person allows the connection to Auto. Without a name there, the person cannot connect their account.

active.description: Conditions on what the tool answered that hold only for an active person of the account, and not for one who was deactivated, has not joined yet or is an app: each a JSON Pointer with the values it may equal, every one of which holds. Put null among the values to let a field that is missing or null pass

sender.description: How Auto reads the person who wrote a message, to know who they are. When Auto reads a person's name before they connect, no message exists: id and sender are the person, and conversation and kind are empty.

chat.description: How Auto answers a person who writes to it where the provider's app reads, for a provider whose destination says under chat which messages a person wrote. Only a provider that ships with the runtime can declare it

renders.description: The name of the render target a message sent through the provider can be written for, where it can be a card the run turns into the layout the provider shows

type.description: The type of the event, as a trigger names it: the reverse domain name of whoever defines the event, followed by their name for it, as in com.example.invoice.paid.

title.description: What happened, in a short sentence a person reads, such as "A message is posted".
What the service calls the place, such as "Channel" or "Repository".

required.description: Whether a trigger must name one place to listen in. Set it to true where a destination made per subscription writes this event's topic from subject.

description.description: How a trigger writes this place, and what must be true there for the service to report it, in a sentence or two an agent is given.

tool.description: A tool of the connection that reads one place, named as the server lists it. The tool must be marked `reads`.

with.description: The tool's arguments. Write {{ subject }} where the place goes: it is filled in with the place as the trigger writes it.

named.description: A JSON Pointer into what the tool answered, to the place's name.

prefix.description: Text to put before the name, such as "#" before a channel's name.

name.description: How Auto reads the name the service gives a place, such as a channel's name, where a trigger writes the place as an id. Leave it out where a trigger already writes the place as its name.

subject.description: The place an event of this type happens in, such as a channel or a repository.

data.description: The JSON Schema of the data an event of this type carries.

types.description: The kinds of events the service reports. Only a provider that ships with the runtime can declare them.

tool.description: A tool of the connection that makes the call, named as the server lists it

with.description: Beside tool, its arguments, written out as they are

method.description: Beside url, the method of an HTTPS request that carries the connection's own credential as a bearer token

url.description: Beside method, the https URL of the request, written out whole

body.description: Beside method and url, the JSON body of the request, written out as it is

id.description: A JSON Pointer into what the call answered, to the account's id

name.description: A JSON Pointer to the account's name, where the answer gives one

identified.description: Where what the call answered names that account

account.description: A JSON Pointer into what the call answered, to the id of the account at the service the connection is for, such as a workspace, where the answer gives one

account_name.description: A JSON Pointer into what the call answered, to the name of the account that the account field identifies, such as the workspace's name. It is read only where account is given. Auto shows this name to a person when they connect their account at the service to Auto.

identity.description: The call that asks the service which account the connection acts as, a tool of the connection or an HTTP request

type.description: How the runtime hears: webhook, an HTTP request the service sends to the runtime's address; websocket, down a socket the runtime opens to the service; queue, into a queue the runtime reads; polling, by calling a tool of the service on a timer and taking what is new

per.description: For webhook and queue, how sending is arranged: subscription, by a call Auto makes for each place requests wait in; app, once on the app at the vendor, for everyone who connects through it

topic.description: Per subscription, the topic, as WebSub names the unit one subscribes to: a Liquid template over with, the arguments of the call that delivered a request, and sent.conversation and sent.id, rendering the place one subscription serves, such as a repository or a chat. The calls subscribe, renew and unsubscribe read it as topic

tool.description: A tool of the connection that makes the call, named as the server lists it

with.description: Beside tool, its arguments, written as the arguments of a function's deliver are

method.description: Beside url, the method of an HTTPS request that carries the connection's own credential as a bearer token

url.description: Beside method, the https URL of the request, written out up to its host, a Liquid template

body.description: Beside method and url, the JSON body of the request, written as with is

id.description: A JSON Pointer into what the call answered, to the id of the subscription it made

expires_at.description: A JSON Pointer to when the subscription lapses, where the answer says

secret.description: A JSON Pointer to the secret the service made for the subscription, where it makes one

subscribed.description: Where what the call answered names the subscription it made

subscribe.description: The call that subscribes, a tool of the connection or an HTTP request

tool.description: A tool of the connection that makes the call, named as the server lists it

with.description: Beside tool, its arguments, written as the arguments of a function's deliver are

method.description: Beside url, the method of an HTTPS request that carries the connection's own credential as a bearer token

url.description: Beside method, the https URL of the request, written out up to its host, a Liquid template

body.description: Beside method and url, the JSON body of the request, written as with is

expires_at.description: A JSON Pointer into what the call answered, to when the subscription lapses now

renew.description: The call that renews a subscription before it lapses

tool.description: A tool of the connection that makes the call, named as the server lists it

with.description: Beside tool, its arguments, written as the arguments of a function's deliver are

method.description: Beside url, the method of an HTTPS request that carries the connection's own credential as a bearer token

url.description: Beside method, the https URL of the request, written out up to its host, a Liquid template

body.description: Beside method and url, the JSON body of the request, written as with is

unsubscribe.description: The call that removes a subscription, without which none is made

lease_seconds.description: Per subscription, the most seconds a subscription lasts before it lapses, as WebSub's lease

needs.description: Per subscription, the group of more of the entry's authorization way whose scopes subscribing takes, where the way's own scope does not cover it

scheme.description: How a delivery proves it is the service's: hmac, a keyed hash of what it sends, in a header; standard-webhooks, signed as the Standard Webhooks specification signs a webhook; bearer, the secret itself, in a header; jwt, a JSON Web Token in a header, signed with the secret

secret.description: Which secret proves it: subscription, the subscription's own, which Auto makes or the service answers when Auto subscribes; app, the app's own, set once on the app at the vendor

hash.description: For hmac, the hash function it keys

signed_payload.description: For hmac, what is signed: {payload}, the body as sent, joined to {timestamp} and {id} where the service signs them, as in v0:{timestamp}:{payload}

signature.description: For hmac, the header that carries the signature, as $request.header.<name>

prefix.description: What the signature or the token starts with before its value, such as sha256= or Bearer and a space

encoding.description: For hmac, how the signature is written

timestamp.description: For hmac, the header or the field of the body that holds when the service sent the delivery

id.description: For hmac, the header or the field of the body that holds the id of the delivery, the same on a retry

token.description: For bearer and jwt, the header that carries it, as $request.header.<name>

alg.description: For jwt, the algorithm the token is signed with, as JSON Web Algorithms names it

when.description: The arrival with which the service checks the address, as filter.when names an arrival

challenge.description: Where the challenge the runtime answers is

response.description: The fields of a JSON answer, each the challenge as it came or its hmac under the destination's secret, by the hash and encoding of its proof; left out, the challenge alone is answered as text

signed.description: Whether the service proves the handshake as it proves a delivery, so that it is answered once proven; false where it comes before any secret exists, as WebSub's verification of intent does

handshake.description: How the service checks the address before it sends, as WebSub verifies intent

tool.description: The tool that lists what is new since the last check. It must be a tool that only reads

with.description: The tool's arguments. They can use `since`, `topic` and `page_token`

method.description: Beside url, the method of an HTTPS request that carries the connection's own credential as a bearer token

url.description: Beside method, the https URL of the request, written out up to its host, a Liquid template

body.description: Beside method and url, the JSON body of the request, written as with is

start.description: The value of `since` for the first check. It can use `now`, so that the first check lists nothing older. When it is left out, the first check reads the newest item and starts from there

list.description: Where the list of items is in the answer, as a JSON Pointer

order.description: The order the tool lists items in: `oldest_first` or `newest_first`

cursor.description: Where in an item the value is that the next check passes as `since`, as a JSON Pointer. When it is left out, the item's id is used

next_page_token.description: Where in the answer the token for the next page is, as a JSON Pointer, when the tool lists in pages

read.description: The call that lists what is new, and how to read its answer

quota.description: The most reads of a conversation the service takes in one window

window_seconds.description: The window, in seconds, from 1 to 86400

clients.description: The client sources whose connections the service limits so, where it limits some apps and not others; left out, every connection

read_limit.description: How often the service lets the replies of a conversation be read, as a rate limit's quota and window: at most quota reads in each window. The runtime reads a conversation no sooner than the window divided by the quota after its last read, on its timer and when the service tells it of a message alike

when.description: The arrivals that make Auto read now: each a runtime expression, a header or a field, with the values it may equal, every one of which holds. Put null among the values to let a header or field that is missing or null pass

subscription.description: Per subscription, where an arrival names the subscription it is for; unlike conversation, it does not narrow which conversations are read

conversation.description: Where an arrival names the conversation it is about, as the answer of a request's delivery names it in sent.conversation, so that only the conversations waiting there are read

automatic.description: Where an arrival holds something only when an app posted the message it is about, which then makes Auto read nothing, as the automatic of conversations passes such a message over

id.description: Where a delivery names the identity of the reply, the one a reading of the conversation lists it by, so that a reply is taken once however often it arrives

sender.description: Where a delivery names who wrote the reply, so that only the person a request waits for can answer it

text.description: Where a delivery holds the reply's words

to.description: Where a delivery names the message the reply answers, as sent.id names a request's message, so that only the request sent as that message can take it

time.description: Where a delivery names when the reply was written, in seconds since the epoch or as an RFC 3339 date-time; it orders the replies that arrive together and decides nothing else

changed.description: Where a delivery holds something only when it is no new message, such as an edit, a deletion or a notice, which then carries no reply and only makes Auto read

reply.description: Where a delivery holds the person's reply, so that Auto takes the reply as it arrives, without reading the conversation first. Only an entry that ships with the runtime can declare it: in a provider added in the configuration file it is refused.

filter.description: Which arrivals make Auto read the conversations that wait, through the reading it does

type.description: The type of event such a delivery is. It must be one of the types declared under types.

when.description: Which deliveries are this event. Each key is a runtime expression into a field of the delivery, and its value lists the values that field may equal. Every condition must hold. Put null in a list to let a field that is missing or null pass.

id.description: Where a delivery holds the event's ID, as one or more runtime expressions whose values are unique together. A delivery is this event only where each of them holds text or a number, so an event the service sends twice has the same ID both times.

time.description: Where a delivery says when the event happened, in seconds since the epoch or as an RFC 3339 date-time.

subject.description: Where a delivery names the place the event happened in.

data.description: Where a delivery holds each field of the event's data, by the field's name.

automatic.description: How to tell that an app or a bot did what a delivery reports: a runtime expression into a field that holds a value only then, or conditions written like those in when. Such an event is marked as one an app or a bot caused.

changed.description: How to tell that a delivery reports no new item, such as an edit, a deletion or a notice: a runtime expression into a field that holds a value only then, or conditions written like those in when. Such a delivery is not an event.

actor.description: Where a delivery names the account that did what it reports, as a runtime expression. It must give the same value as the id that identity answers for that account, so that the two can be compared.

own.description: Two runtime expressions: the field that names the account that did what a delivery reports, and the field that names the account the connection acts as. Where both name the same account, the connection did it itself, and the delivery is not an event.

topic.description: The topic Auto subscribes to for this event in one place, as a Liquid template that reads subject, the place the event happens in. It must render the same topic as the destination's own topic renders for a request waiting in that place. Each event of a destination made per subscription needs one, and no other event takes one.

items.description: One kind of delivery that is an event, and the fields of the delivery that hold the event's ID, time, place and data.

events.description: Which deliveries are events the service reports. A delivery is the event of the first item it matches. On a polling destination, it says which listed items count as events, and an item becomes the event of the first entry it matches. Only a provider that ships with the runtime can declare them.

kind.description: What kind of message it is: mention, a message that names the app; direct_message, a message written to the app alone; ambient, a message the app can read that does not name it. Auto takes an ambient message only where it is a reply in a thread.

when.description: Which deliveries are a message of this kind. Each key is a runtime expression into a field of the delivery, and its value lists the values that field may equal. Every condition must hold. Put null in a list to let a field that is missing or null pass.

id.description: Where a delivery holds the message's ID within its conversation, as a runtime expression.

conversation.description: Where a delivery names the conversation the message was written in, such as a channel.

thread.description: Where a delivery names the first message of the thread the message was written in, when it was written in one.

sender.description: Where a delivery names the person who wrote the message.

account.description: Where a delivery names the account of the person who wrote the message, such as their workspace: one or more runtime expressions, read in order, the first that holds text naming it.

text.description: Where a delivery holds the words of the message.

time.description: Where a delivery says when the message was written, in seconds since the epoch or as an RFC 3339 date-time.

automatic.description: How to tell that an app or a bot wrote the message: a runtime expression into a field that holds a value only then, or conditions written like those in when. Such a delivery is no message a person wrote.

changed.description: How to tell that a delivery reports no new message, such as an edit or a deletion: a runtime expression into a field that holds a value only then, or conditions written like those in when. Such a delivery is no message.

shared.description: Where a delivery says whether the conversation is shared with another organization, as a runtime expression into a field that is false where it is not. Where the field is missing, the conversation is taken as shared.

own.description: Where a delivery names who wrote the message, and where it names the app's own user, as two runtime expressions. When both name the same user, the app wrote the message itself, so it is not a message a person wrote.

items.description: One kind of message a person writes where the app reads, and the fields of the delivery that hold the message.

chat.description: Which deliveries are messages a person wrote where the app reads, and of which kind. A delivery is the message of the first item it matches. Only a provider that ships with the runtime can declare them.

account.description: Where an arrival names the vendor's account it happened in, such as a workspace, so that Auto finds the connections made in it

user.description: Where an arrival names the vendor's user it is for, where the service sends for each person

connection.description: For a destination of the app, where an arrival names whose connection it is for

kind.description: For queue, the queue the service delivers into, by its vendor's name for it

method.description: The method of the HTTPS request that answers the socket's address, carrying the app's credential as a bearer token

url.description: The https URL of that request, written out whole

address.description: A JSON Pointer into what the request answers, to the socket's wss address

open.description: How the runtime finds the address of the socket it opens

credential.description: For websocket, the value of the app that opens the socket, named as the vendor names it, such as app_level_token: an app credential of the entry's secret way, sent as a bearer token with the request of open

acknowledge.description: For websocket, where a message names the id the runtime acknowledges it by

heartbeat_seconds.description: For websocket, how often the service asks the runtime to send it a heartbeat, in seconds

destinations.description: The ways the service sends what happens where a request waits, in the order the runtime tries them. There is one of each type, except polling, which may have one for each read. An event is heard through the first destination that reports it and that the runtime can take. A request's replies are heard through the first the runtime can take.

title.description: The label of the field a person gives the value in, in at most 40 characters

format.description: uri for a value that is a whole address, an https URL or an http URL on a loopback address, which stands only as the whole url of an mcp provider

placeholders.description: The values that differ from one connection to the next, by name: each a description with a pattern and an example, or with choices

name.description: The name a tool and a consent that asks more name the group by

for.description: What the group is for, in one sentence of the person's words

scope.description: The scopes it adds to those the way asks, separated by single spaces

says.description: What a connection can do through each scope it adds, by the scope

ending_codes.description: For authorization, the error codes beside invalid_grant with which the token endpoint refuses a refresh because the consent has ended, so that the connection is broken rather than failing

url.description: The https URL where the start, the hand-off and the end of a connection made through it are asked

connections.description: The aud of the note the gateway takes with the start, the hand-off and the end of a connection

calls.description: The aud of the note the gateway takes with a call

claims.description: What the note may carry beside the ids: name and playbook_name, the person's and the playbook's display names, and takes_answer, true on the note of a call that delivers a request, which takes an answer; ids alone where it is left out

gateway.description: For authorization, the gateway a connection is made through: it makes the consent with its own client, keeps the vendor's tokens, and hands the runtime a key of the connection's own, sent under the security scheme name names

permissions.description: For authorization and secret, whether a connection made this way acts as the app, application, or as an account at the service, delegated; delegated where it is left out

account_types.description: The kinds of account at the service that a connection made this way may act as, on a way with delegated permissions. service is an account the company made for automations. personal is the account of the person who connects. Both when it is left out.

refresh_token_expires_in.description: For authorization, how long the provider keeps a refresh token, in seconds, a whole number above 0, after which the person signs in again; it states what the provider imposes, and Auto enforces nothing from it

title.description: The label of the field a person gives the value in, in at most 40 characters

format.description: uri for a value that is a whole address, an https URL or an http URL on a loopback address, which stands only as the whole url of an mcp provider

placeholders.description: The values a connection made this way takes beside the provider's, by name, asked only when this way is chosen: each written as a placeholder of the provider is, and held in this way's addresses or its base_url

base_url.description: For openapi, the https URL the calls of a connection made this way go to, in place of the provider's base_url and of the server its document names, each {name} in it a placeholder

subject.description: For jwt_bearer, the account the token is asked for, such as a mailbox, each {name} in it a placeholder of the way or of the provider

key_file.description: For jwt_bearer, where the two values sit in the key file the service gives, each as a JSON Pointer. Auto keeps the private key, sealed, and records the client's ID; it keeps nothing else of the file

instructions.description: For secret, how a person makes the key, in Markdown without HTML of at most 1,000 characters: where it is made, the plan or role it needs, the permissions it needs and its format

key_page.description: For secret, the https address of the page where a person makes the key; for client_credentials, of the page where a person makes the client; for jwt_bearer, of the page where a person makes the key file; for authorization, of the page where a person makes the organization's own OAuth client

key_page_title.description: For secret, client_credentials, jwt_bearer and authorization, the label of the button that opens key_page, such as Create your Tracker app, in at most 40 characters

title.description: The heading of the step, in at most 60 characters

instructions.description: What the person does in the step, in Markdown without HTML of at most 1,000 characters

key_page.description: The step of the page where the key is made, above the button to key_page

title.description: The heading of the step, in at most 60 characters

instructions.description: What the person does in the step, in Markdown without HTML of at most 1,000 characters

page.description: The https address of the page of the service where the person does the step

page_title.description: The label of the button that opens page, in at most 40 characters

items.description: A step the person does on a page of the service

pages.description: The steps the person does on other pages of the service, in order, after the step of key_page and before the step of the key, at most 4

title.description: The heading of the step, in at most 60 characters

instructions.description: What the person does in the step, in Markdown without HTML of at most 1,000 characters

key.description: The step of the key, above its field; the page shows its instructions in place of the way's instructions

title.description: The heading of the step, in at most 60 characters

instructions.description: What the person does in the step, in Markdown without HTML of at most 1,000 characters

connected.description: What the person does once the connection is connected, shown after approving

steps.description: For secret, client_credentials, jwt_bearer and authorization, the heading and paragraph of each step of the page where a person approves the connection, each a title and instructions; for authorization, the steps of making the organization's own OAuth client, shown where the connection goes under it

example.description: For secret, what a key looks like, with an ellipsis in place of its characters, such as ghp_…, which the field of the key shows

pattern.description: For secret, beside example, the regular expression from ^ to $ every key matches, of at most 200 characters, by which the runtime refuses a value of another format

name.description: Its name, as the vendor names it, such as app_level_token, by which a websocket destination of the entry names it as its credential and give_credential's app_credentials takes it

description.description: What a person reads of it: the label of the field it is given in, beside the field of the key

title.description: The heading of its step on the page where a person approves the connection, in at most 60 characters, above its instructions

instructions.description: How a person makes it, in Markdown without HTML of at most 1,000 characters, which its field shows

key_page.description: The https address of the page where a person makes it

example.description: What it looks like, with an ellipsis in place of its characters, which its field shows

pattern.description: Beside example, the regular expression from ^ to $ every such value matches, of at most 200 characters, by which the runtime refuses a value of another format

app_credentials.description: For secret, the app credentials a person may give beside the key, such as an app-level token, each optional to them, in the order the page shows them; one is offered only where a websocket destination of the entry names it and the runtime opens sockets, and the runtime keeps each sealed as it keeps the key

test.description: For secret, the tool that checks a key: a tool that needs no arguments and is marked reads, which the runtime calls once with the key a person gives before it keeps anything; a key the service refuses is refused, and where the call ends any other way than in a result the runtime keeps nothing and answers that the key could not be checked

client_id_title.description: For client_credentials and authorization, the label of the field a person gives the client's id in, as the service names it, in at most 40 characters

limitation.description: What a connection made this way cannot do, in one sentence of at most 160 characters, which a person reads under this way where they connect the app.

credentials.description: The ways a credential reaches the server, in the order a person is offered them, the first the default, at most one of each kind, secret, client_credentials, none, authorization or jwt_bearer, with each of application and delegated permissions; a way that asks a scope says, beside it, what a connection can do through each scope, and an authorization way that asks a scope may name in more the groups of scopes a later consent may add to it

replaces.description: The providers this one replaces, by name: where both are served, no way of a provider it replaces is offered, a connection made from one is not used, and reconnecting such a connection adds it again from this provider under its name

items.description: A way the runtime receives what a connection's service sends: http, a webhook, an HTTP request the service sends to an address of the runtime, taken only when it proves it is the service's

receive_events.description: The ways the runtime receives what a connection's service sends, of http; every way when left out, and none for an empty list, so a request is answered only through Auto or by reading its replies. CONNECTIONS_RECEIVE_EVENTS wins over it

connections.description: What people may add as connections through their agents, tool servers of an org which every playbook of the org may use; the clients whoever runs the runtime registered at authorization servers, and whether Auto's clients serve as well; and the providers it adds beside those the runtime ships. CONNECTIONS wins over it

usage_ping.description: Whether the runtime sends its anonymous usage ping when it starts: its release, the operating system, the processor, the version of Node.js, how it was installed and a random install id, and nothing of its work. On when left out; DO_NOT_TRACK or SCARF_NO_ANALYTICS in the environment turns it off too. USAGE_PING wins over it

payload_offloading.description: Whether a payload larger than payload_size_threshold_bytes, the input, output or answer of a run, the prompt its record holds, a definition's document or a value a workflow holds, is offloaded: kept once in the content store, the ledger's database or the bucket of CONTENT_STORE_URL, and named in its record by its SHA-256 and its size, as the claim check pattern does. On when left out. Turning it off keeps new payloads in their records and still reads those offloaded before. PAYLOAD_OFFLOADING wins over it

payload_size_threshold_bytes.description: The size in bytes of UTF-8 past which a payload is offloaded, from 2048 to 65536; 16384 when left out. A change applies to new payloads alone. PAYLOAD_SIZE_THRESHOLD_BYTES wins over it

key.description: The key Studio gave as the account holder or an organization admin registered this runtime, written as a reference to the variable that holds it, such as ${LICENSE_KEY}. AUTO_RUNTIME_LICENSE_KEY wins over it

allocation.description: The offline credits an operator of Auto signed for a runtime that does not reach Auto, the JSON of their payload, signature and kid, written as a reference to the variable that holds it, such as ${ALLOCATION}. AUTO_RUNTIME_ALLOCATION wins over it

license.description: The license of this runtime, which runs it on its org's credits past the 100 free runs and the free rate of 15 runs a UTC day and 75 a UTC month it runs without one: its key, and the offline credits of a runtime that does not reach Auto. AUTO_RUNTIME_LICENSE wins over it

package.description: The package of the extension, which the server imports by its name

integrity.description: The integrity of the installed package, sha512- and the base64 of the SHA-512 of its files; a package whose files differ stops the start
